options: It uses the RIGHT SEPARATOR for whatever OS it runs on - hand-built backslashes break on macOS/Linux
explanation: Portability by default. GetFileName, GetExtension and GetTempPath round out the family.

stem: For a 10 GB log file, the right reader is:
options: File.ReadLines - it STREAMS lazily in constant memory
explanation: ReadAllLines loads everything; ReadLines is an IEnumerable<string> yielding one line at a time - 3.5's laziness with a disk behind it.

stem: ReadAllLines -> Where(not blank) -> Split(',') -> Select(new Score(...)) -> ToList() is:
options: The lines->split->objects->query shape behind half of all data-wrangling scripts
explanation: A simple CSV read is Module 3 applied to a file. Learn the shape once, reuse forever.

stem: Reading a file whose FOLDER does not exist throws:
explanation: Missing file vs missing directory are different exceptions; UnauthorizedAccess and IOException (locked, disk full) complete the usual set.

stem: A StreamWriter outside a using, when an exception hits, leaves:
options: The FILE LOCKED (and possibly unflushed) until a later GC finalises it
explanation: 4.8's lesson applied: the OS handle outlives its usefulness. using guarantees flush-and-close on every path.

options: JSON TEXT - the bridge between objects in memory and files/wires
explanation: Serialisation is how anything gets saved or sent. Deserialize<T> reverses it - records are the perfect partner (2.9).

options: Throws JsonException - external data is never trusted data
explanation: Catch JsonException at the boundary, and remember 4.5: nullability annotations do not survive the wire - validate after.

stem: record Player(..., List<string> Inventory); loaded == original after a JSON round-trip is FALSE because:
options: List<string> compares by REFERENCE inside record equality - two lists, same contents (2.9's trap)
explanation: The data survived fine; the equality is telling the truth about lists. SequenceEqual compares contents when it matters.

stem: new JsonSerializerOptions { WriteIndented = true } is for:
options: HUMAN-READABLE output - config files, save files people might inspect
explanation: Pretty-printing costs bytes and buys debuggability. Machine-to-machine wires usually skip it.

stem: File.Exists before ReadAllText covers the common case, but you still handle exceptions because:
options: The file can vanish or lock BETWEEN the check and the read - and permissions can deny you
explanation: Check-then-act has a gap (a race - 6.1's theme in miniature). The check avoids the ordinary case; the catch covers the rest.
